answers.answer: Reveal a shuffled region card for the King’s region. Each player takes another region card for their home region and places their Grande there. Their ten initial Caballeros go as follows: two in the home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: “reveal the top card and put the King in that region”; “two in their home region… one… on the first space… seven in their court”.

answers.answer: Players choose the first-round starter. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts playing power cards. Others play clockwise, and no power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Players choose who begins… later, the player who took the last turn… begins. Others play clockwise. No value already played this round may be matched.”

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on your power card from provinces into court; recruiting fewer is allowed. Recruitment happens before choosing an available face-up action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Take turns in descending power-card value”; “At the start of your turn recruit up to…”; “After recruitment, choose an available face-up action card.”

answers.answer: If your provinces do not have enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region cannot supply pieces, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “you may take your own from the board to make up the difference”; “King’s region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.”

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves Caballeros from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo. You may divide the allowance among destinations. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: “maximum”; “from your court to any regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely.”

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment and the special action may be done in either order, but each activity must be completed as a whole before beginning the other; neither can be split or interleaved. You may decline the special action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Do them in either order… neither may be split or interleaved. You may decline the special action.”

answers.answer: After taking a turn, lay aside the selected action card so later players cannot choose it. After all players take a turn, discard any face-up action cards left. The King card is revealed each round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Lay aside the selected action card”; “discard any remaining face-up action cards”; King card “never permanently discarded.”

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region, and special actions do not override this taboo. The region may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment and protected locations: “no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it”; “It may still be scored”; moving the King “changes which region is protected.”

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. King location does not restrict entry: Caballeros may go there regardless of the King’s location. They leave only during general scoring; no action removes them earlier.
answers.evidence: “Announce clearly how many you put inside”; “may go into the Castillo, regardless of the King’s location”; “leave only during general scoring.”

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. First, before uncovering the Castillo, each player secretly selects one board-region destination for all their Castillo Caballeros, excluding the King’s region. Second, score the Castillo. Third, reveal disks and move all Castillo Caballeros to their owners’ chosen regions (an illegal King-region choice sends them to that player’s court), then replace the empty Castillo. Fourth, score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points. Destinations are chosen before the Castillo is revealed.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages: “Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo”; then “Score the Castillo”; “Reveal disks and empty the Castillo”; then “Score the nine regions.”

answers.answer: A player cannot split their Castillo Caballeros: all go to one chosen region. The King’s region is not a legal destination, and the pieces cannot be kept in the Castillo. If it was chosen illegally, those pieces go to that player’s court.
answers.evidence: General scoring: “All that player’s Castillo Caballeros must go to one region”; King’s region “prohibited”; “none may be retained inside or split”; illegal choice sends pieces “to their court.”

answers.answer: On 5/3/1 with counts 4,4,4,3, the three tied leaders each score 3 and the next player scores 1. Grandes do not count toward the majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Publisher example: “counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1”; “Only Caballeros count… A Grande… contributes zero Caballeros.”

answers.answer: On 6/4/2 with counts 4,3,2,2, scores are 6,4,0,0.
answers.evidence: Publisher example: “On 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.”

answers.answer: In a two-player game only first place can pay; in a three-player game first and second can pay. A tie shifts to the next rank’s value, then the player-count cutoff applies. Thus a two-player tie for first pays neither player.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: “Two players: only first place… Three players: only first and second”; “a two-player tie for first pays neither player.”

answers.answer: The King’s bonus is +2 for the sole majority holder when the King’s region is scored. The home bonus is +2 for the sole majority holder who has their own Grande in that region. Bonuses apply whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scoring. Neither is awarded on a tied first place.
answers.evidence: Bonuses: “King’s bonus: +2 for the sole majority holder”; “Home bonus: +2 if the sole majority holder has their own Grande”; “Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.”

answers.answer: Special scoring of the Castillo does not empty or redistribute it. Uncover and score it, then cover the same Caballeros again; redistribution waits until general scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: “score it, then put the Castillo over the same Caballeros; redistribution waits until general scoring.”

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It cannot move into or out of the King’s region, cannot be stacked on the other scoreboard, and must stay right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0; it cannot be rotated to change its values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: “Castillo is allowed”; “No movement into or out of the King’s region”; scoreboards “cannot be stacked”; “never reversed or rotated.”

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King’s region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King’s region. Other Grandes may already be in the destination. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: “Move your Grande to another region except the King’s region or Castillo. It cannot leave the King’s region. A destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.”

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which card you choose, though taking the visible top card will be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: “any one… including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which.”

answers.answer: The standard game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins.
answers.evidence: End: “Finish all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. Whoever is furthest along the success track wins.”

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down beside the board. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round (five face-up choices). The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Separate action cards into stacks… Shuffle each stack separately”; “Start the round marker at 1”; Turn Structure: “Reveal the top card of each of the five action stacks.”

answers.answer: A played power card does not return to your hand; it remains in your face-up used stack. Only the top card of that stack is visible. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Played cards remain in each player’s face-up used stack with only the top card visible, rather than returning to hand.”

answers.answer: If you move the King before ordinary deployment, the King’s new position determines adjacent deployment destinations; if deployment is done first, use his old position. The King card may place the King in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: deploy after King movement using his “new position”; Stack 5: put the King in “any region except Castillo.”

answers.answer: Put the Veto card before you and retain it to stop one special action during the current or next round. It cannot stop another card’s ordinary deployment.
answers.evidence: Veto: “Put the card before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion.”

answers.answer: While a Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as a player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or stop the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed, and any already executed parts are not undone; you may veto only part.
answers.evidence: Veto: “must announce special actions”; “Object as soon as the player starts”; completed actions “cannot be vetoed”; already executed parts “are not undone.”

answers.answer: Discard the Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: “Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.”

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces. A player with an empty court sends none. The selecting player is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: “Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; an empty court sends none. The selecting player is unaffected.”

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces, because they send all they have if fewer than three. The selecting player with five is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Decay — three from court: fellow players send “three… or all they have if fewer than three”; “selecting player is unaffected.”

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and printed card require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Begin with the player to the selecting player’s left, continue clockwise, and the selecting player goes last. Each takes their own pieces from any regions and/or court, never from the King’s region or Castillo. The heading differs by saying “fellow players.” No shortfall rule is given if someone has fewer than three eligible pieces.
answers.evidence: The King returns: “each player, including the selecting player, sends three own Caballeros”; order is left, clockwise, selecting player last; heading instead says “fellow players.”

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each piece to its owner’s provinces. Pieces cannot come from courts, the King’s region, or the Castillo. No fallback is specified if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one from a region for “each player, including themselves”; no court, King’s region, or Castillo; no explicit fallback.

answers.answer: Affected fellow players secretly choose one region on their disks; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. A chosen region must contain at least two of that player’s Caballeros, and they return two to the provinces. If a player has any legal region with at least two, the choice must be such a region; the summary does not state that the player may choose a singleton region instead.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: “secretly chooses one region… choices simultaneous and revealed together. It must contain at least two… return two.”

answers.answer: If the player has at most one of their Caballeros in every region, choose a region containing one and return that one to the provinces. The summary does not provide a fallback for no eligible pieces.
answers.evidence: Singleton fallback: if “at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.”

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region containing at least one of their Caballeros, then choices are revealed together; they return all their own Caballeros from that region to the provinces. A player with no Caballeros in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all: simultaneous secret disk selection, region with “at least one,” return “all their own there”; player with none is unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes. Choose any region, including the King’s region or the Castillo, and use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; they are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Pick one region: “including the King’s region or Castillo”; normal scoring, rank limits and bonuses; Castillo “cover the same pieces again.”

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia, Catalonia, and Seville, but eligibility uses the current first value when mobile scoreboards are present. Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify; Granada with 4/0/0 does qualify. Applicable home and King’s bonuses apply to these special scorings.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions: current first value is 4; printed group listed; 8/4/0 in Galicia removes it and 4/0/0 in Granada adds it. Stack 3 bonuses apply.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country, Aragon, and Valencia; the 6-and-7-value group is Old Castile, New Castile, and Granada. Current first values determine eligibility, so a mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for category eligibility. Castillo is explicitly excluded from all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 table lists the printed groups, says current first value determines groups and mobile scoreboards replace printed values, and says “Castillo is not scored” for all 5-value regions.

answers.answer: Only a sole first-place holder scores; a tie for first scores nothing, and lower ranks score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First position only: “Only sole first places score; other ranks get nothing. A tie for first scores nothing… Excludes Castillo.”

answers.answer: Score all board regions tied for the most total Caballeros. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros than either tied region.
answers.evidence: Region(s) with most: compare totals in each board region; score all regions tied for most; “Castillo is neither considered nor scored.”

answers.answer: Compare only nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and the Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Region(s) with least: “Compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for the least. Empty regions and Castillo are neither considered nor scored.”

answers.answer: The acting player chooses a region, and each fellow player moves all their own Caballeros out of it. Each affected player secretly chooses another region on their disk; choices are revealed simultaneously and their group moves there. If a player chooses the King’s region or the region being vacated, their pieces go to their court instead. Castillo cannot be emptied by this card. The summary does not reconcile Castillo as a potential disk destination with the general rule allowing movement into Castillo, so that case is unsupported and needs clarification.
answers.evidence: Movement: “all fellow players move all their own Caballeros out”; destinations by simultaneous disks; choosing King’s region or vacated region sends them to court. Edge cases note the source does not reconcile Movement’s disks with permission to move into Castillo.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King into a neighboring region, at most one region away. The King card can put him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: “neighboring region, no more than one region away”; King card: “any region except Castillo.”

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to your court. This is separate from the 4-stack card’s ordinary deployment of up to four Caballeros from court to the board; each activity is completed separately, and either may go first. No shortfall procedure is given if provinces cannot provide both.
answers.evidence: The Court: “Move two of your own Caballeros from provinces to court”; separate from “ordinary up-to-four court-to-board deployment; either… can go first”; no shortfall procedure.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on their disks and reveal simultaneously. Score each uniquely chosen region under normal rules. Any region chosen by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: Each secretly chooses a region to score: “All players choose secretly on disks and reveal simultaneously”; uniquely chosen regions score; duplicates do not.

answers.answer: You may split your own Caballeros from one region among other regions and/or the Castillo, and may return some to the original region. The origin excludes the King’s region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King’s region but may include Castillo. The express permission to return to the origin applies to this action.
answers.evidence: Intrigue: “Take all your own from one region and distribute among other regions and/or Castillo. You may return some to the original region”; origin exclusions and destination restrictions stated above.

answers.answer: The special action adds up to two more of your own Caballeros from court, for up to three total when combined with the normal one-Caballero deployment. The additional two may go to any non-King region or Castillo; only the normal deployment requires adjacency to the King.
answers.evidence: Intrigue “Two more from court”: “With the normal one, up to three enter the board, but only the normal one requires adjacency”; special destinations are any non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may choose only one special alternative: either add up to two more from court or move all your own Caballeros from one region. The normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice card: “Choose one of the preceding special actions, not both. Normal deployment still applies.”

answers.answer: Move up to five Caballeros from one origin region; they may be your own and/or foreign, but cannot come from multiple origin regions. They may be distributed to other non-King regions and/or the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue “Up to five from one region”: own and/or foreign from “one origin region,” distributed to “other non-King regions and/or Castillo.”

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros, choosing fewer if desired, from any non-King board regions, including multiple origins. Your own pieces cannot be included, and the Castillo cannot be a source. Destinations may be any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue “Any three foreign”: up to three other players’ Caballeros from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: For any three, move up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. For any four, move up to four own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The three-piece card says any regions; the four-piece card says other regions.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table: Any three allows own/foreign from any non-King origins to any non-King destinations; Any four allows own/foreign from any non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. Pieces may come from any regions. Under the general Intrigue rules, origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo, while destinations exclude the King’s region but may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue: “Up to two of your own plus two foreign… separate ownership allowances”; general Intrigue origin and destination restrictions.

answers.answer: Move up to four of your own Caballeros only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo cannot be a source.
answers.evidence: Intrigue “Any four of your own”: “own only” from non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; general origins exclude Castillo.

answers.answer: On the 4-stack each-player secret scoring action, players may choose any of the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not the Castillo; only uniquely chosen regions score. By contrast, the card where its player picks one region to score allows any region, including the King’s region or Castillo, with normal scoring rules.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: disk has nine board regions “including the King’s region, but not Castillo”; Stack 2 pick one region: any region “including the King’s region or Castillo.”

answers.answer: Both mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The place-or-move action may introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place both mobile scoreboards beside the board”; Stack 4: “Introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on it to a different region.”
